inventoryAsset.label: Inventory asset
inventoryAsset.help: Debited when stock arrives, credited when it leaves. Your balance-sheet stock value.

cogs.label: Cost of goods sold
cogs.help: Debited when a sales invoice is posted, for what the goods that left actually cost. Point this at your COGS account — an invoice will not post without it.

grni.label: Goods received not invoiced
grni.help: Credited on every goods receipt. Nothing clears it automatically any more — settle it with a journal entry when you pay the supplier, or it will keep accruing.

inventoryAdjustment.label: Inventory adjustment
inventoryAdjustment.help: The counter-account for corrections, theft and anything not otherwise routed. An expense account is right here — opening stock has its own account on the Behaviour tab, because it is value the business started with rather than a cost it incurred.

stockVariance.label: Stock variance
stockVariance.help: Count differences, rounding residue and cost variances land here.

scrapWriteOff.label: Scrap / write-off
scrapWriteOff.help: Used for damage, expiry and sample write-offs. Falls back to Inventory adjustment.

salesRevenue.label: Sales revenue
salesRevenue.help: Credited when an invoice is posted, for the value of the goods sold. Required before an invoice can post.

accountsReceivable.label: Accounts receivable
accountsReceivable.help: Debited by an invoice and credited by a customer receipt. The company-wide default: a customer can be given an AR account of their own on their record, but never a per-category one — a receivable raised on one account and settled against another would never clear.

customerDeposits.label: Customer deposits
customerDeposits.help: A liability account (e.g. 2010 Customer Deposit). A receipt taken before the invoice exists is credited here rather than to receivables, and moves to receivables when you apply it to an invoice. Leave it unset and advances credit Accounts receivable as before.

outputVat.label: Output VAT payable
outputVat.help: Credited with the VAT charged on an invoice. Required as soon as any line carries a tax rate.

salesDiscounts.label: Sales discounts
salesDiscounts.help: Contra-revenue: debited with discounts given, so the gross and the discount are both visible. Leave it unset and discounts are simply netted off revenue instead.

salesReturns.label: Sales returns & allowances
salesReturns.help: Contra-revenue: debited when goods come back, so gross sales and the returns rate stay readable on the income statement (e.g. 4010). Leave it unset and a return reduces the original revenue accounts instead, which balances but hides the returns figure entirely.

serviceRevenue.label: Service revenue
serviceRevenue.help: Credited for lines whose product is a service. Falls back to Sales revenue.

fxGainLoss.label: Foreign exchange gain / loss
fxGainLoss.help: Where the difference goes when a document is settled at a different rate than it was raised at (e.g. 7100). Only needed if you trade in more than one currency — without it, such a settlement is refused rather than left unbalanced.

loyaltyPointsPayable.label: Loyalty points payable
loyaltyPointsPayable.help: What customers' unspent points are worth. Credited as points are earned, debited as they are spent or expire.

loyaltyExpense.label: Loyalty & promotion expense
loyaltyExpense.help: The cost of points given away, and of wallet top-up bonuses. Expired points come back off it.

customerWalletPayable.label: Customer wallet payable
customerWalletPayable.help: Money customers have loaded onto their e-wallet and not yet spent.

rentalDepositsHeld.label: Rental deposits held
rentalDepositsHeld.help: Security deposits taken against rented equipment. Owed back to the customer, so a liability — and kept apart from customer deposits, which can be spent on any invoice.

rentalIncome.label: Rental income
rentalIncome.help: Rent invoiced on equipment rental contracts.

rentalDamageRecovery.label: Rental damage & loss recovery
rentalDamageRecovery.help: Fees charged when rented equipment comes back damaged or does not come back.

codGetFile.title: Get File books the COD receipt
codGetFile.help: Tick a courier to book its orders' receipt the moment Pay Status becomes Get File (the courier has collected the money and sent its file): Dr 1210 COD receivable (courier) / Cr Sales Revenue, plus cost of goods sold, dated that day. A later Paid books nothing more — the courier's payout is recorded on Accounting › COD Remittances when it reaches the bank. Unticked couriers book the receipt when the order is marked Paid, as before.

codMethods.title: COD payment methods
codMethods.help: Tick the Pay By methods that mean the courier collects the money. An order paid by one of them opens Settle Payment, Record Receipt and a Checkout Paid save with អ្នកដឹកប្រមូល (COD) ticked, so its receipt is booked to 1210 COD receivable (courier) until the courier's payout is recorded on Accounting › COD Remittances. The box can still be changed on each order. With nothing saved here, a Method named COD counts.

Receipts, deposits and delivery fees go here when nobody picks an account: it is pre-selected in the Settle, Deposit, Delivery Fee and Record Receipt forms, and used by bulk Paid, the Orders Management drawer and Customer Payment › Post Now. A Cash method still goes to Cash on Hand, and a COD receipt stays on the courier's account (1210). Automatic keeps today's choice (the bank account).
